## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

I want you to build a first-person shooter at the level of the most recent Call of Duty games. It should be utterly perfect, visually beautiful, with every single thing done at AAA quality—from textures to physics to anything you could think of. Fan out sub-agents and have sub-agents tackle each one individually so that the game is utterly perfect. Have a separate sub-agent check each item visually to ensure it looks triple A. That separate sub-agent should be a really harsh critic, and if it doesn't look triple A, keep iterating until it does. Don't stop until each sub-agent is utterly wowed with the quality when compared with the actual Call of Duty game. It should literally compare them side by side blind and say which one looks better. Do this in ThreeJS. Continue iterating until it's utterly perfect. Fan out sub-agents and ultracode.
# 🤯 OMG — Oh My GitHub ### 🚀 One Prompt In. A Full Game or App Out. 🚀 [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-🔥%20works-brightgreen?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/denaidark/OhMyGithub?style=for-the-badge&logo=github)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/issues) [![GitHub Actions](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub%20Actions-automated-2088FF?style=for-the-badge&logo=githubactions&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![OpenCode](https://img.shields.io/badge/powered%20by-OpenCode-111111?style=for-the-badge)](https://opencode.ai/) ```text ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ DESCRIBE IT → BUILD IT → TEST IT → PLAY IT ║ ║ ║ ║ One GitHub issue. One prompt. A complete project. ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ ``` **No API keys to configure. No server to maintain. No local setup maze.**
--- ## 🤯 What Is OMG? > **Your GitHub issue becomes the product brief.** OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. Add the `OpenCode` label to the issue. 4. Let GitHub Actions build, test, verify, and propose the result. ```text Your idea → GitHub issue → OpenCode → tests → immutable OmGithub project ``` ## ⚡ Quick Start Create an issue in your repository with a concrete request: ```text Build a neon asteroid game. Requirements: - Arrow-key movement - Score and restart button - Win and lose states - Responsive browser layout - Run tests and verify it in a browser ``` That is the whole user-facing workflow. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit. To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a `branch: ` directive. The directive selects the checkout and is removed before the issue body is sent to OpenCode: ```sh gh issue create \ --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \ --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \ --body "Build a tiny browser page." \ --label Goal \ --label OpenCode ``` The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. If the directive is absent, the repository default branch remains the target. ## 🌍 What Can You Build? | 🎯 Use case | ✨ Example | |---|---| | 🎮 Arcade games | Breakout, Space Invaders, Asteroids, Match-3 | | 🧩 Puzzle games | Word games, logic puzzles, card games | | 🏃 Interactive demos | Physics experiments, simulations, visual toys | | 📊 Dashboards | Filters, charts, status panels, analytics views | | 🛠️ Internal tools | Trackers, generators, small workflow apps | | 🌐 Landing pages | Product pages, portfolios, interactive showcases | | 🧪 Prototypes | Turn a product idea into a runnable proof of concept | | 📱 Browser apps | Responsive tools that work on desktop and mobile | ## 🧰 What Happens Automatically? > **The workflow is the product.** - 📥 Checks out your repository and the shared OpenCode skills. - 🏷️ Synchronizes `model/*` and `skill/*` labels. - 🧭 Reads issue labels to select the model and requested skills. - 🤖 Runs OpenCode against the current project. - 🧪 Runs a second verification prompt after implementation. - 🌐 Starts the app and checks the local runtime. - 🔗 Creates a temporary public preview URL when verification passes. - 🔀 Creates and pushes an `opencode/` branch. - 🕹️ Adds an `Open Project` link backed by the repository path, with full-commit links retained for compatibility. - 💬 Posts progress and access details back to the issue. - 🧹 Cleans up temporary tunnels and runner processes. ## 🏷️ Model and Skill Labels Labels let you control the workflow without editing YAML. ```text model/opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free skill/load-sketchfab-threejs skill/gauntlet-loop ``` The workflow validates the selected labels, passes them into OpenCode, and records the resolved model and skills in the run logs. Shared skills are discovered from: ```text .agents/skills//SKILL.md ``` ## 🔄 OpenCode Workflow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Trigger] --> B[Prepare project] B --> C[Run build.md] C --> D[Run verify.md] D --> E{Public app works?} E -- No --> F[Run public-app-fix.md] F --> E E -- Yes --> G[Run completion-report.md] G --> H{Screenshots exist?} H -- No --> I[Run screenshot-evidence.md] I --> H H -- Yes --> J[Commit and push] J --> K[Create immutable project link] K --> L[Publish report] L --> M[Complete] ``` ## 🏗️ Architecture ```text ┌──────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ │ GitHub issue │ ──▶ │ GitHub Actions │ ──▶ │ OpenCode │ │ + issue text │ │ runner + labels │ │ + .agents │ └──────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ └──────┬───────┘ │ ┌─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ Build code Run tests Verify app │ │ │

content.text:
So this is an OMGithub project: given one prompt, build a complete browser game. The prompt: "rpg survival tycoon tower defense (mythological and biblical references)".

I should build a polished, playable browser game in the repo root (index.html, plus JS/CSS). Vanilla HTML/JS likely best — no build step, easy.

Let me plan a game concept that combines RPG, survival, tycoon, tower defense with mythological/biblical references:

**"Covenant: Fallen Pantheon"** — You are a steward of a sacred sanctuary at the edge of the Flood. Waves of mythic/biblical enemies (locusts, scorpions, Nephilim, plague shades, etc.) attack. You place relics/towers (Ark Arrow, Cherubim Ember, Brazen Serpent, Manna Well, Solomon's Seal), gather resources (Manna, Gold, Faith), level up your Champion (RPG), unlock skill tree, survive 20 waves, tycoon economy (build & upgrade generating income), tower defense placement on a grid/path.

Need to deliver something visually impressive and functional, with verification via playwright and screenshots.

Scope realistically: single-page canvas game, vanilla JS modules. Features:

- Title screen with animated background, start button, instructions.
- Core loop: top-down map with a winding path. Waves of enemies follow path toward Sanctuary (gate). Player places towers on build slots, spends gold; towers auto-attack. Player hero (RPG) maybe moves with WASD and attacks/casts abilities? That adds complexity but boosts "RPG" feel. Could include a controllable champion near the path using WASD and mouse click to attack; simpler: hero stands at gate, auto-attacks with a holy smite ability on click.

Actually a tower defense with RPG hero controlling is ambitious but doable. Let's design:

**Resources:**
- Gold (from kills, tycoon buildings) — used for towers/upgrades.
- Manna (income) — generated by Manna Wells, used for hero skills/level? Maybe simplify: Gold only, plus Faith resource generated by shrines for hero abilities/global buffs.
- Souls/XP for hero levels.

**Tycoon element:** guardians (towers) generate tribute each wave; build economy structures ("Manna Well", "Reliquary", "Oracle") that produce gold per wave. Upgrade them.

**RPG element:** Hero "the Covenant Bearer" levels up from XP, choose from 3 boons at level-up (roguelite card choices), hero has HP, can move/attack with mouse? If hero dies, revive after cooldown/penalty.

Simplest engaging control: Hero auto-attacks nearest enemy in range; player uses 3 abilities bound Q/W/E (Smite AoE, Ward shield, Judgement beam) with cooldowns/mana, and can reposition hero with click? maybe movement via WASD limited to central courtyard.

Tower defense: fixed path, 12 build pads along path. Click pad, select tower type from panel, build. Upgrade/sell via click on built tower. Enemies with types: Runner (Locust swarm), Tank (Nephilim), Flyer? Flying enemies need anti-air. Bosses (Leviathan, Behemoth, Goliath, Serpent, Angel of Death?). Each wave themed.

Waves: 20 waves, boss at 5/10/15/20. Between waves prep timer or "Begin Wave" button; tycoon income at wave end.

Visuals: Canvas 2D with rich gradients, glow, particles, screen shake, floating damage numbers. Isometric-ish? Keep top-down but with tile layout and path styling. Use nice fonts (Google fonts might not load offline — maybe use system serif fallback; but network likely available. Better use local safe fonts with CSS, e.g., 'Cinzel' via Google Fonts with fallback). Capture may load fonts; if network blocked, fallback serif fine. Could avoid external deps to guarantee offline. Use CSS font stacks: Georgia / serif for mythic vibe; maybe embed no fonts.

I can create SVG sprites inline for towers/enemies drawn procedurally with canvas shapes — actually procedural drawing with gradients and glows can look great. Draw units as symbolic shapes: locust small triangle with wings, Nephilim big hulking polygon, scarab etc. Add animated path shimmer, sanctuary gate with columns, clouds/smoke.

Audio: WebAudio synthesized ambient drones + SFX (no assets). Add mute button. Nice touch, but ensure no autoplay issues; start on user interaction.

UI: left/top HUD with resources, wave, sanctuary HP; right panel tower shop; bottom hero bar with HP/mana/abilities and level. Responsive layout for desktop and mobile; mobile: canvas scaled, panels overlay. Need a start overlay with title and CTA.

Verification: run local server on port 3002? The start.sh uses runtime script and PORT env. Playwright-cli instructions mention http://localhost:3002. I'll start via runtime start script with PORT=3002 in tmux/background. Then use playwright-cli screenshot, maybe write a Playwright script for interaction testing (place tower, start wave, inspect state). Could use playwright-cli directly (it's a CLI). Let's check its help later.

Need tests. The runtime expects npm? Root has no package.json; index.html projects are served statically. I can add a test script using node --test for pure game logic, if I structure logic in a module importable in Node. That's good practice and verifies economy/wave logic. Structure:

- index.html
- styles.css
- src/game.js (main, browser)
- src/logic.js (pure functions: wave definitions, damage calc, upgrades, economy) exportable ESM; game.js imports it. Tests: tests/game.test.js using node:test with dynamic import.

Keep dependencies zero.

Given the huge scope, I need to be efficient but produce quality. Let me design concretely.

## Game design: "COVENANT — The Last Bastion"

Tagline: "Command a dying sanctuary. Hold the line against myth and prophecy."

Setting: The Flood has swallowed the world. Your citadel, Mount Zion's last terrace, guards the Gate of Eden. Legions of myth and scripture march to unmake it.

Core screen:
- Canvas 1600x900 logical, scaled to fit.
- Dark cosmic background with stars, distant ark silhouette, rain? Ash particles.
- Map path: winding S-curve from top-left spawn to bottom-right/center gate. Path drawn as glowing stone road with runes.
- Build pads: ~10 circular rune pads along path.
- Hero at gate area (fixed position?) with attack range; player can move hero along a small arena? Let's let hero be movable with WASD across map but constrained? If hero moves over path, enemies could attack? Enemies only target gate; hero damages them. Hero can be attacked by ranged enemies/boss AoE? Keep enemies focused on gate; hero has HP but only loses in certain events? RPG without death risk is weak.

Alternative: hero is placed on the battlefield and enemies attack hero if in proximity. If hero HP hits 0, hero is "cast down" and revives after 10s; gate takes damage meanwhile. Movement with WASD adds action. Enemies target gate primarily but melee attack hero if hero within 60px. Boss has AoE that damages hero. That's enough.

Hero auto-attacks nearest enemy within 190px every 0.7s (holy bolts). Abilities:
- Q: "Smite" — AoE 140 radius at cursor or around hero, 90 damage + stun 1s, 18 mana? cooldown 6s.
- W: "Aegis" — shield 3s absorbing damage + heal? cooldown 14s.
- E: "Judgement" — beam to cursor, 8s cooldown, big damage line.
- R: "Resurrection"/"Manna Rain"? Ultimate at level 5: "Plague of Light" damages all enemies on screen, cooldown 45s.

Mana regenerates. Level ups from XP give boon choices (3 cards) paused overlay.

Tycoon: gold income buildings:
- Manna Well: +8 gold per wave, cost 60.
- Reliquary: +14 per wave, cost 110, unlocks after wave 2.
- Oracle's Tent: +22 per wave, cost 180.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable browser game from the user's one-line prompt: "rpg survival tycoon tower defense (mythological and biblical references)".

## Requirements
- Combine RPG, survival, tycoon economy, and tower-defense mechanics.
- Use mythological and biblical themes/characters.
- Deliver a working browser game (HTML/CSS/JS) in the repository, visually polished, tested, and verified in a browser.
- User gave no additional detailed requirements.

## Decisions
- Game concept: **"COVENANT — The Last Bastion"**; defend a final gate through 20 waves against mythic/biblical foes.
- Core loop: build guardian towers on rune pads, build tycoon economy structures in sanctum courts, control an RPG hero with abilities, level up and choose roguelite blessings, survive bosses.
- Tech: vanilla ES modules, Canvas 2D, procedural art/audio, no assets or build step.
- Key layout: WASD/click-to-move; abilities Q, **C** (Aegis, to avoid W movement conflict), E, R; shop hotkeys 1–7.
- File structure: `index.html`, `styles.css`, `src/logic.js`, `src/audio.js`, `src/game.js` (concatenated from `src/parts/01-core.js` … `06-input.js`), tests planned under `tests/`.
- Verification: start server on port 3002 via `PORT=3002 ./start.sh` in tmux session `covenant`; use Playwright headed Chromium/Xvfb.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented full game data/rules in `src/logic.js`: path/pads, 9 enemy types, 4 towers, 3 economy buildings, 20 authored waves, 14 blessings, abilities, geometry/economy/upgrade helpers.
- Implemented procedural audio engine in `src/audio.js` (ambient drone, SFX, mute handling).
- Implemented full HTML UI in `index.html` with inline SVG icon sprite, title/help/pause/boon/end overlays, HUD, armory, hero bar, wave banner, toasts, tooltips.
- Implemented extensive responsive styling in `styles.css`.
- Implemented game engine in `src/game.js` (~4520 lines) covering static art, rendering, combat, waves, bosses, hero abilities, boons, shop/economy, input, UI updates, debug API.
- Syntax check passed: `node --experimental-default-type=module --check src/game.js`.
- Dev server running successfully on `http://localhost:3002` (curl returned 200).
- Screenshots directory created at `screenshots/`.

### Active
- Browser verification just started; `playwright-cli open` failed because it expects `/home/runner/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium-1243/chrome-linux64/chrome`, but installed build is `chromium-1248`.

### Blocked
- Playwright CLI version 0.1.19 expects chromium-1243 while cache has chromium-1248; workaround options: use `--browser chrome` (`/usr/bin/google-chrome`), `--config` pointing at a config with channel `chromium`/executable path, or invoke Playwright directly from `~/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/node_modules/playwright`.
- No gameplay/visual verification or screenshots captured yet.

## Next Move
1. Open the game with a working Chromium: try `DISPLAY=:0 playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002 --browser chrome` or pass a config specifying installed Chrome/chromium executable.
2. Capture title screenshot to `screenshots/title.png`, then click `#startBtn`, capture gameplay.
3. Check `playwright-cli console` for runtime errors; fix any JS/CSS issues.
4. Test placing towers/economy, starting a wave, hero movement/abilities, boons, pause/help, victory/defeat via the exposed `window.__covenant` debug API (`fill()`, `advance()`, `autoRun()`).
5. Run `window.__covenant.autoRun(20)` to validate the full 20-wave loop and balance; fix failures.
6. Inspect screenshots visually; iterate on layout/visual quality (desktop 1440×900 and mobile 390×844).
7. Add focused tests under `tests/` using `node --experimental-default-type=module --test tests/`; verify and commit changes.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game.js`: final concatenated game engine (generated; edit parts then re-concatenate).
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/parts/01-core.js`: imports, DOM refs, state, static background/path art, resize helpers.

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

# COVENANT — The Last Bastion

A browser RPG / survival / tycoon / tower-defense game about holding the final gate while myth and scripture tear the world apart. Twenty waves, nine mythic foes, seven guardian and sanctum relics, and roguelite blessings — all drawn and scored procedurally with no assets or build step.

<!-- omgithub:readme:start -->
## 🚀 Build, play, and remix with OMGithub

**Remixed using [OMGithub.com](https://omgithub.com).**

[![OMGithub](https://img.shields.io/badge/OMGithub-Open%20project-orange?style=for-the-badge)](https://omgithub.com/PuzzleRabbit/PlayGround)
[![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source-181717?style=for-the-badge&logo=github)](https://github.com/PuzzleRabbit/PlayGround)

- 🎮 [Open the project](https://omgithub.com/PuzzleRabbit/PlayGround).
- ✨ [Remix this project](https://omgithub.com/?remix=PuzzleRabbit%2FPlayGround).
- 💻 [Explore the source](https://github.com/PuzzleRabbit/PlayGround).
- 🛠️ [Check build runs](https://github.com/PuzzleRabbit/PlayGround/actions).
- 🐛 [Report an issue](https://github.com/PuzzleRabbit/PlayGround/issues).
- 👤 [Explore the creator's projects](https://omgithub.com/PuzzleRabbit).
- 🌍 [Create with OMGithub](https://omgithub.com).
- 🧬 [Explore the remix source](https://omgithub.com/?remix=PuzzleRabbit%2FPlayGround).
<!-- omgithub:readme:end -->

## The covenant

- **RPG** — Control the Covenant Bearer with WASD or click-to-move. He attacks on his own and unlocks Smite, Aegis, Judgement, and Wrath of Heaven.
- **Survival** — Every foe that reaches the Gate breaks a seal. At zero seals, the run ends.
- **Tycoon** — Raise Manna Wells, Reliquaries, and Oracle Tents in the sanctum courts. They pay tribute at the end of each wave.
- **Tower defense** — Place four kinds of guardian on rune pads, then upgrade or sell them. Slow, poison, armour pierce, and range auras reward smart placement.
- **Roguelite** — Level up and choose one of fourteen blessings; no two runs need take the same shape.

## Play

- **WASD / arrows / click** — move the Bearer
- **Q** — Smite, **C** — Aegis, **E** — Judgement, **R** — Wrath of Heaven
- **1–7** — choose a guardian or sanctum relic
- **Space** — sound the horn and begin a wave
- **F** — toggle game speed, **M** — mute, **P / Esc** — pause, **H** — field manual

Portrait phones are asked to rotate; the battlefield is designed for landscape.

## Run locally

```bash
PORT=3002 ./start.sh
```

Open `http://localhost:3002`. The game is plain HTML, CSS, and ES modules — no install or build step.

## Tests

The rules layer has no DOM dependencies and is covered by Node's built-in test runner:

```bash
node --experimental-default-type=module --test tests/logic.test.js
```

## Structure

- `index.html` — interface, overlays, and inline icon set
- `styles.css` — responsive gold-and-ink art direction
- `src/logic.js` — pure data and rules (waves, towers, economy, blessings)
- `src/audio.js` — procedural Web Audio score and effects
- `src/game.js` — the canvas engine
- `src/parts/` — readable source sections that concatenate into `src/game.js`
